summary: Intermittent SSE/WebSocket disconnects causing truncated streaming outputs and unclear reconnect behavior
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NoteWise reports intermittent stream interruptions when using server-sent events (SSE) and WebSocket streaming for text-generation. The client sees partial output (truncated tokens) and the client SDK automatically attempts to reconnect but resulting resumed streams either duplicate fragments or resume from a later token — producing incoherent final outputs.

Impact:
- Affected customer: NoteWise Analytics (dedicated tenant on us-east)
- Several production jobs for realtime summarization fail to produce coherent final responses; customer reports ~8% of streaming calls in the last 24h were affected.
- Business impact: loss of generated text quality, increased retries, potential downstream data corruption for archived transcripts.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted Dedicated capacity (us-east GPU pool d-42)
- Client SDK: notewise-js v0.8.3 using EventSource for SSE and native ws for WebSocket fallback
- Models observed: gpt-redwood-13b (primary), gpt-redwood-7b-q4 (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Initiate streaming chat generation with streaming=true, max_tokens=1024, and a long prompt (~8k chars).
2) On SSE path expect token-by-token events.
3) After ~3-10s, stream stops with no final_done/event. Client receives no final finish event but receives a close event on the underlying TCP connection.
4) SDK attempts reconnect (backoff 250ms) and receives a resumed partial sequence which either overlaps existing tokens or jumps ahead.

Observed logs (customer provided):
- client: "event: message\ndata: {\"token\":\"the quick brown\" }\n...\nevent: close\n"
- server (gateway): "WARN connection=conn-7b2d: downstream reset while streaming to tenant=notewise code=ECONNRESET"
- streaming-proxy: "DEBUG stream-session=ss-324: resumed session after 312ms, last-kv=0x1a3, resume-offset=576"

Additional context:
- Customer uses long-running sessions with KV cache enabled. They previously reported a separate issue (SUP-4689) about occasional duplicate tokens during canary rollouts; might be related.

Request from customer:
1) Root cause analysis for disconnects and explanation of reconnect semantics for SSE vs WebSocket in our platform.
2) Short-term mitigation and recommended SDK changes/workarounds to avoid partial outputs.
3) Long-term fix plan and ETA.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:12 - Support (Ethan Rivera): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE for immediate investigation; requesting request IDs and sample request timestamps from the customer.

2026-03-12 10:27 - Customer (NoteWise - Maya Chen): Provided three sample request IDs and a short screen recording of the client behavior. Request IDs: req-20260312-77a, req-20260312-81f, req-20260312-90b. Noted that failures spike during peak ingest between 09:00-11:00 EDT.

2026-03-12 11:03 - SRE (Aisha Patel): Investigating streaming-proxy logs and gateway traces for the provided req IDs. Found ECONNRESET events for two of the three requests; correlating with a transient overload on the d-42 GPU pool at 10:05 EDT.
investigation_notes:
Summary of checks performed:
- Correlated request IDs against gateway and streaming-proxy logs; two requests show TCP resets during active token streaming.
- Checked node-level metrics for pool d-42: observed CPU scheduling spikes and elevated network retransmits at 10:04-10:06.
- Streaming-proxy reports resume-offset values that do not match last-sent token offset for the session; suspect mismatch in resume token bookkeeping when there is an in-flight cache eviction.
- Reviewed SDK behavior: notewise-js v0.8.3 will attempt reconnects and requests a resume token header; if resume fails, it opens a fresh session but merges messages naïvely which can create duplicate fragments.
- No evidence of auth/permission failures. No error codes from model process; model continued producing tokens until process closed the connection.

Hypothesis:
1) Under transient resource pressure (GPU or network), the serving runtime or the streaming proxy can force-close downstream TCP connections (ECONNRESET) to preserve headroom.
2) The streaming-proxy's resume bookkeeping for long sessions with KV caching has an off-by-one condition when an eviction or compaction occurs mid-stream, returning an incorrect resume-offset.
3) The client SDK's reconnect merge strategy is insufficiently defensive: it attempts to stitch resumed tokens into the existing buffer without verifying server-provided sequence numbers, causing duplicated/truncated outputs.

Immediate investigative artifacts:
- Gateway trace links: https://internal-ops.redwood/gateway/traces/req-20260312-77a
- Streaming-proxy debug snippets: captured in /var/log/streaming-proxy/2026-03-12-10.log (attached to ticket in the console)
resolution_notes:
Short-term mitigations applied (2026-03-13):
- Applied a temporary throttle on intensive background jobs in pool d-42 to reduce transient overloads.
- Pushed a server-side guard in streaming-proxy: if ECONNRESET occurs mid-stream, mark session as non-resumable and emit an explicit final_error event to clients to avoid silent truncation. Deployed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proxy/pull/214 (hotfix v0.9.1).
- Notified NoteWise to upgrade notewise-js to 0.8.4 which includes safer reconnect handling (verify server sequence numbers before merging; prefer fresh session if server indicates resume gap).

Long-term plan:
1) Implement robust resume token verification and stronger invariants in streaming-proxy to ensure resume-offset is validated against last-sent token metadata (ETA: 2026-03-27).
2) Add server-side telemetry for resume success/failure rates and surface on Redwood Console per-tenant streaming health (ETA: 2026-04-10).
3) Improve SDKs: a) default to conservative reconnect behavior for long sessions, b) expose hooks for app-level idempotency/merge strategies (ETA: 2026-03-31).

Customer communication and next steps:
- 2026-03-13 09:00 - Support (Ethan Rivera): Notified NoteWise of the hotfix and recommended SDK upgrade. Asked customer to run a 2-hour smoke test during non-peak window and share results.
- Follow-up: monitor resume-related telemetry and reopen if recurrence >1% in next 7 days.

Ticket status: awaiting customer confirmation of SDK upgrade smoke test. If customer still observes issues, SRE will attach full pcap and escalate to runtime team.
final_resolution: Pending customer smoke test confirmation. Hotfix deployed to streaming-proxy and SDK patch released. Root cause likely combination of transient pool overload causing ECONNRESET and a resume-offset bookkeeping edge-case in the streaming-proxy; SDK reconnect merge behavior made the symptom worse. Full server-side resume validation planned.
